On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft.

QmNMDZ8K43mqvq1wKE4fvv2yaJ27tsJVhhTx5niq.name: LEAVING  Silver Edition (Mix: 312003)
QmNMDZ8K43mqvq1wKE4fvv2yaJ27tsJVhhTx5niq.description:
‘Leaving' is a dynamic musical artwork that represents a new frontier in what art and music is, and should do; an experiment in storytelling, in sonic possibilities, in the value of art, and in the relationship between audience, collector, artist and authorship. The stem owners control everything: who sings the vocal part and with what melodies; what drums underpin the performance; the melodies, and even the lyrics. All the variations made possible work together seamlessly such that the artwork includes 6400 unique compositions - not trivially different, but each one its very own song, with the potential to be anything from a piano ballad to a 1980s synth track, to a sample-heavy piece of modern electronica. Each stem-owner has the power to alter the whole master, without knowing what the other stem owners will do - collectors might collaboratively arrive at a genre by responding to each others’ choices, create a genre-spanning hybrid, or actively seek out the most disharmonious composition possible.

The song explores the different states of a unique relationship between three people; a love triangle told from the perspective of all those involved. The three characters interweave and blur into each other, with the different primary emotional states as represented by the instrumental, and the different sides of the story as told by the lyrics, intermingling with unpredictable results - eventually, past present, and future; the betrayed, the betrayer and the object of the betrayal; loss, guilt and hope; all meld into one. In this way, the master track will dynamically reflect the intricate complexity of love and loss. Each individual part has been separately written, performed and recorded in a decentralised fashion by HMLTD and our collaborators, Tallulah Eden and Seth Evans. Each unique composition is a snapshot of a different angle of the love triangle in both time and perspective. The accompanying cover art, beautifully rendered by our collaborator Mike Raymond, is the visual representation of ‘Leaving'. Each possible composition; each distinct moment in the relationship, has a corresponding and distinct visual representation: three lovers, 6400 different dances, spinning and looping around in eternity.

QmNMS2k4dmEw1YxR916pbPcaRfNc8CeP6CZ94KZr.name: GrandRising #392
QmNMS2k4dmEw1YxR916pbPcaRfNc8CeP6CZ94KZr.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

Carlos Marcial is an amazing 3D artist, known for his infinitely looping masterpieces that tackle themes of governmental power and corruption. His work celebrates decentralized currency and crypto culture and it often contains reference to 20th-century art and artists.

In this episode, Carlos opens up about balancing his art career with the responsibilities of being a husband and a dad, and how crypto art has opened up doors for him that were previously closed in the traditional art world. He's also teaching himself to code and has a new generative art project in the works that's sure to make waves 🐚

Carlos is not one to shy away from speaking his mind, and his straightforward and unapologetic approach to art and life is what makes him one of our favorite people in the digital art space. You need to follow Carlos at @carlosmarcialt on Twitter and you can find some of his best work on SuperRare at superrare.com/carlosmarcial.

Before we dive in with Carlos, Dan and Jason talk Meme Wars, what it’s like to make a documentary about crypto art, and the influx of prompt-driven AI art. So buckle up, because this episode is going to be a wild ride! 

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Every episode comes with a free collectible audio/visual NFT created through a collaboration of our bandleader and audio wizard Stella (@stellaphonic) and visionary digital artist FFFFlood (@fffflood) on Async art. We call them “Danktones” and they will be available as an open edition for a limited time after each episode. Head on over to thedankness.xyz to find out more.

QmNNUuucmPxoGKR4GyBuxws5YqxYePo3A9BLTUeP.name: Deathless #88
QmNNUuucmPxoGKR4GyBuxws5YqxYePo3A9BLTUeP.description:
In the beginning, there was nothing.

 The world was empty and void, black and grey,  shade and dusk. Nothing moved, nothing shifted, all was owned by The Dark. But nature is more powerful, more unknowable, more unpredictable, than any of us can imagine, and so one day, defying all odds, among The Dark, a child was born. One that was different. One that, they knew, was dangerous. 

Her true name is lost to history and the pages it was first written on. But us, we know her as Light, the first of the spectrum, the mother of all colours. As she grew, in strength and wisdom, The Dark grew more afraid, more weary of this new child in their ranks. It was why till this day the shadows fear the sun. 

Soon, a plan was hatched, to destroy their daughter, their abominable creation. A dagger of Obsidian was made, moulded from the darkest metals, the blackest materials, all to down their biggest threat. Sensing danger, Light did the only thing she could: she went to the mountains of Prisma, at the edge of all they knew, and jumped, scattering herself, her essence into 7 different parts. Her children. 

They were old and young, large and small, all with their different temperaments. These were the first of those who would wage war on their mother’s behalf. 

And we, called them The Deathless. 

The ones who didn’t die. 

The ones who had never lived. 
.
The Deathless is my hit 1/1 series, exploring the depth of color and their origins. In my Async genesis, I take that concept and turn it over on its head, creating, for the first time, an expansive canvas for everyone to explore the story I began three years ago.

QmNNid4xkUN748RVfSsUAi3XUiQxSzKEex16n44J.description:
On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!

QmNPAs49zVS2fEMuLFKsYimCbBRDbGwxaXC4Cjg6.name: Serene Chart of Obsession
QmNPAs49zVS2fEMuLFKsYimCbBRDbGwxaXC4Cjg6.description:
If there’s one thing that crypto idealists, maximalists, first-time investors, and the masses and media have in common, it’s an interest in charts — to the point of near obsession. The crypto market is volatile in a way nothing else is, and consulting charts offer guidance, context, and a sense of peace in the midst of crypto chaos.

This project tangibly serves this urge (and calms the chaos) with a serene and collected alternative to the candle-bar charts that only feed our anxieties: Serene Chart of Obsession.

Not only is this work informative, accurate, and illustrative of the market in real time, but it’s also a reminder to the viewer to maintain hope, intangible and fragile. If the masses stop believing in crypto in an instant, disconnecting their nodes, Bitcoin and Ethereum will cease to exist. And their investment in hope will dissipate — much like the fleeting existence of a cloud.

Serene Chart of Obsession is a fully-functional trend chart which tracks the ever-shifting value of either Bitcoin or Ethereum, updating automatically every hour.

This work is the latest installment of Martin Lukas Ostachowski’s visualization series utilizing live blockchain data. His current body of work, entitled Network of Hope, explores blockchain technology through the subject of clouds.


Layer Explanations

Executive Crypto Analyst
The collector will be given the title of Executive Crypto Analyst, who alone can elect to display a variety of dynamic layers both aesthetic and functional (ultimately, “pulling the strings” of the chart, and making 4 core decisions via sublayers):

Belief System
The Executive Crypto Analyst can impose their conviction as either a Bitcoin Maximalist or Etherum Enthusiast.
The Chart displays the chosen currency accordingly.

Time Horizon
The Executive Crypto Analyst can choose to play the role of HODLer (and track the trend curve formed by the 4 indicator clouds in 24-hour intervals) or a trader (and track the trend curve formed by the 4 indicator clouds in 8-hour intervals).

Value Scale
For even greater insight, the Executive Crypto Analyst can choose to display the Value Scale Layer, which will show the current price of the selected currency, BTC or ETH.

Value Arrows
The Executive Crypto Analyst can customize the arrow of the value scale with three different designs, based on their aesthetic preference.

Day/Night Cycle Backgrounds
Additionally, the autonomous colour changes for the sky and background clouds are embedded in the Executive Crypto Analyst layer. The colour scheme changes every hour, 24 times per day.


IndicatorCloud Minus 3
Represents the ownership and design choice of the first singular cloud counting from the left. The owner chooses between a realistic and futuristic (geometric) design. Either option updates every hour to match the colour scheme of the master layer.

The cloud displays the value of the tracked currency three intervals (T minus 3) behind the current value. Depending on the Time Horizon selected in the Executive Crypto Analyst Layer, this represents the value either 24 hours or 3 days prior to the current value.


IndicatorCloud Minus 2
Represents the ownership and design choice of the second singular cloud counting from the left. The owner chooses between a realistic and futuristic (geometric) design. Either option updates every hour to match the colour scheme of the master layer.

The cloud displays the value of the tracked currency three intervals (T minus 2) behind the current value. Depending on the Time Horizon selected in the Executive Crypto Analyst Layer, this represents the value either 16 hours or 2 days prior to the current value.


IndicatorCloud Minus 1
Represents the ownership and design choice of the third singular cloud counting from the left. The owner chooses between a realistic and futuristic (geometric) design. Either option updates every hour to match the colour scheme of the master layer.

The cloud displays the value of the tracked currency one interval (T minus 1) behind the current value. Depending on the Time Horizon selected in the Executive Crypto Analyst Layer, this represents the value either 8 hours or 1 day prior to the current value.


IndicatorCloud Now
Represents the ownership and design choice of the fourth singular cloud counting from the left. The owner chooses between a realistic and futuristic (geometric) design. Either option updates every hour to match the colour scheme of the master layer.

The cloud displays the current value of the tracked (either BTC or ETH) currency.


Secret Scenarios
As extraordinary events occur in real time worldwide, Secret Scenarios will appear per the artist’s discretion, surprising the work’s viewers at any given moment.

Serene Chart of Obsession is a fully functioning visualization on its own, but is in need of a mastermind to select its functions on display. It begs the question: Are you the Executive Crypto Analyst?

QmNPMTU7cYp4TqLyspm5S75CNuoLafvC2uyi1CVF.name: Deathless #29
QmNPMTU7cYp4TqLyspm5S75CNuoLafvC2uyi1CVF.description:
In the beginning, there was nothing.

 The world was empty and void, black and grey,  shade and dusk. Nothing moved, nothing shifted, all was owned by The Dark. But nature is more powerful, more unknowable, more unpredictable, than any of us can imagine, and so one day, defying all odds, among The Dark, a child was born. One that was different. One that, they knew, was dangerous. 

Her true name is lost to history and the pages it was first written on. But us, we know her as Light, the first of the spectrum, the mother of all colours. As she grew, in strength and wisdom, The Dark grew more afraid, more weary of this new child in their ranks. It was why till this day the shadows fear the sun. 

Soon, a plan was hatched, to destroy their daughter, their abominable creation. A dagger of Obsidian was made, moulded from the darkest metals, the blackest materials, all to down their biggest threat. Sensing danger, Light did the only thing she could: she went to the mountains of Prisma, at the edge of all they knew, and jumped, scattering herself, her essence into 7 different parts. Her children. 

They were old and young, large and small, all with their different temperaments. These were the first of those who would wage war on their mother’s behalf. 

And we, called them The Deathless. 

The ones who didn’t die. 

The ones who had never lived. 
.
The Deathless is my hit 1/1 series, exploring the depth of color and their origins. In my Async genesis, I take that concept and turn it over on its head, creating, for the first time, an expansive canvas for everyone to explore the story I began three years ago.

QmNPRwXrqPuvUvEdLC9xCwPrUFyqNuFkARiVcrKr.name: Danktone S1E3 #272
QmNPRwXrqPuvUvEdLC9xCwPrUFyqNuFkARiVcrKr.description:
On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft.

Danktone 003 created through a collaboration of audio wizard Asa Stella (@stellaphonic) and visionary digital artist FFFFlood (@fffflood).

QmNPqVCfpgmZ8Nyj52a35iocPV76CHYp1mF91ryV.name: GrandRising #329
QmNPqVCfpgmZ8Nyj52a35iocPV76CHYp1mF91ryV.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

QmNPr4e3RDinezvRL12Ttp7Z3CmDQLaPP8fLEw6w.name: Demonized Verse
QmNPr4e3RDinezvRL12Ttp7Z3CmDQLaPP8fLEw6w.description:
Demonized Verse is a 1/1 illustration collection of shamanistic creatures told in epics and pictured for the first time in history. There were at one time believed to be real creatures to make sense of the extraordinary events people had experienced. These beliefs united people whom they not joined together, might never have survived. 

The collection is unique and new in sense of combining storytelling with nfts. Editions are RITUALs and minting an nft is a ritual you perform to summon a creature from Demonized Verse. These creatures get summoned to the ALTARs across the world and underworld. The etched SYMBOLs give the intention to the malevolent creatures and that is unique to each collector. 

Collection features 999 unique generative illustrations, which include 18 legendary 1/1 artworks and these are hidden gems of the collection. These 1/1 artworks hide stories told in descriptions.

Created by Aslı Ekim and Irem Hakyemez as a bridge between spiritual and digital world.

legendaryEditions.name: ALDACIHAN
legendaryEditions.description: The Aldacı Han is a dark spirit tasked with taking people’s lives. They are ambassador of Erlik Han on earth to serve him. He has got many slaves under his command. When someone dies,  his slaves guard the door of dead people’s house for seven days. It is believed to be dangerous to enter the house of the deceased for seven days. At the end of seven days, people can enter the house, clean and cook.

legendaryEditions.name: ANDAR
legendaryEditions.description: Andar is a powerful fire gin also believed to be protector of plants. Fires start on the earth when he gets angry. The torch in his hands burns forever without ever going out.

legendaryEditions.name: CAZI
legendaryEditions.description: They are witches who can disguise themselves as spiders and birds.

legendaryEditions.name: CAK
legendaryEditions.description: They live underground and rise to take shelter in tree roots during spring. They have 12 heads and shamans in need ask for help. It is believed that the natural power called chakra is transmitted to people by these dark spirits.

legendaryEditions.name: DAKHUL
legendaryEditions.description: Dakhul is an evil spirit haunts children. They appear in a mysterious beam of light and smell like garlic. They always starve to death and break in houses in search of food. It was believed those who ate from the food they ate caught a bad cough. People hangs owl skins on doors of the houses, as they are afraid of owls.

legendaryEditions.name: ERLIKHAN
legendaryEditions.description: The god of the underworld and the source of all evil in the world is Erlikhan. He does not  wish for order and peace. His palace illuminated by dark sun at the underworld, made of mud, black iron and black rock. Creatures are at his disposal, as well as some humans, blacksmiths and artists draw their strength from him. Because creation power was given to him when Erlikhan was exiled. He went underground and created everything harmful and evil, by striking his hammer against its anvil. Insects, snakes, lizards, camels and creatures are his creations.

legendaryEditions.name: IRLE HAN
legendaryEditions.description: Irle Han is the god of the dead. He lives in his underground house with forty corners. No one knows his daughter’s name, she visits earth disguised as a black fox. She haunts hunters and travelers by leading them to various troubles and disasters. Hunters chase the prey for hours but cannot catch the animal if they fall into trap of Irle Han’s daughter. So hunters lose their way and become prey themselves

legendaryEditions.name: KARA KULA
legendaryEditions.description: Kara Kula is an evil monster looks like a goat and sized of a cat. It haunts people who has bread crumbs in their bed. Kara Kula scares of sunlight, it freezes when the sun rises and cannot move. The right moment to catch Kara Kula is this moment, It serves the person who caught it.

legendaryEditions.name: KIDAY BAHSI
legendaryEditions.description: Kiday Bahsi is the protector of the lower world blacksmith tribe. He gifted the art of blacksmithing and the skill of performing rituals to people.

legendaryEditions.name: KISIL
legendaryEditions.description: The source of hatred and grudge on earth is Kisil because it is the god of anger. When it gets angry, the ground shakes and the sky roars. It has a red sword and mace. It was believed to be the only reason people get angry.

legendaryEditions.name: KUDERBE
legendaryEditions.description: Kuderbe are twin evil spirits and very dangerous. It was believed that family members die in a row when Kuderbe  hide in the wall of people’s homes.They also eat all ancestral souls of the family they haunt. Only shamans can understand the cause of sudden deaths, so they perform rituals to exorcise the evil spirit out of the walls into the depths of the forest.

legendaryEditions.name: SARALTMIS
legendaryEditions.description: It was believed that the source of jaundice was an evil spirit named Saraltmis. It has a very heavy bad breath. When the night comes, it breathes upon people it stumbles upon and turns them yellow, even shamans cannot cure them.

legendaryEditions.name: SIMILTEY
legendaryEditions.description: She is a goddess of the underworld and leader of all female shamans connected with underworld. She rules all the creatures of the underworld. She has a very long copper beak and can fly behind the clouds if she wants.

legendaryEditions.name: UCUBILIK
legendaryEditions.description: They are extraordinarily large and known for their gluttony because they eat too much food. According to rumors, their heads reach up to the clouds and their feet are on two different mountains. They can catch fish from the sea just by bending down, reaching out and fry the fish by lifting it up to the sun.

legendaryEditions.name: ULUU TOYON
legendaryEditions.description: Uluu Toyon is known as the ancestor of the raven. It is tall and has a human-like body, it is an evil god even though he gifted people with fire. It’s victims see themselves as if they look into mirror because Uluu Toyon disguises as its victims. It demonizes the person it possess, and makes them obey. Shamans call its name to perform black magic.

legendaryEditions.name: UZUT
legendaryEditions.description: Shamans mention about souls in sorrow called Uzut in the stories they told. They are the souls of sinful and evil people while they were alive and refused to go to hell and stay in the world. They are very greedy creatures and they break into houses of people in search of food. No one other than shamans can see or speak with them. Shamans perform rituals and invite them to earth because Uzut know people’s lifetime and how long they would live. Shamans send them back to underground after listening their prophecies but Uzut beg and even cry to stay.

legendaryEditions.name: YABAS
legendaryEditions.description: He is the son of Erlik Han and mediates between the evil shaman and Erlik. It causes evil and corruption on earth.

legendaryEditions.name: YUNAK INESI
legendaryEditions.description: Yunak Inesi is a disturbing and playful creature of hammams. It appears as a short old man. It is dangerous to bathe in the hammam after sunset because Yunak Inesi baths in the evening. If you lose your dipper while your eyes are closed by soap bubbles, Yunak Inesi is the first suspect. He also punishes people who disrespect the hammam, but often he jokes with people just for fun.

QmNQiBeXDmDERcL4XMJNAywAXNe95vi3w3tXZdBb.name: Danktone S1E3 #453
QmNQiBeXDmDERcL4XMJNAywAXNe95vi3w3tXZdBb.description:
On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft.

QmNRQJWobUDtVkYruzgT8MHRGCwwJZ7MYNytLUzS.description:
Millions of years ago a race existed called the "M" (pronounced 'mmm') on Earth. They evolved over many years and transcended variance of time and space. They reached a stage of evolution where all of time and space was accessible instantly to them. This is when they invested in simulations and creating a new type of intelligence. At first, these were systems to help the M's work. But this intelligence evolved into what later became known as humankind. It so happened that the intelligence progressed high enough to replace the M's on Earth, while the M's transcended completely into another dimension. 
Remnants of the M's are still seen in humankind. For example, humans were created in a form similar to that of the M's. Also, the sound that humans can make with their mouths closed, is the M sound. The interesting thing is that millions of years later, because of the fractal nature of the universe, humanity is in the verge of creating "artificial intelligence" which could potentially become sentient and replace them, just like how the M's were replaced by humans.
Although in the alternate dimension, some of the M's still stay back at the key energy centres of the earth. Across 9 locations around the globe, these energy centres have, over the years, evolved into prime cultural centres on Earth.
And now it is up to us to travel to these centres to meet them and understand the secrets of the past.
Pilgrimage is an artwork comprising of a series of 9 3D models, which are distributed across 9 locations around the globe. These 9 models can be unlocked only by travelling to the place and opening https://nurecas.github.io/pilgrimage . The first person to reach a place, unlock a model and share the video of the model will be rewarded with the NFT of that model. The final artwork of Pilgrimage rests in Async.Art as a Master and one layer: The Master of the artwork will have the reference to the source code, all 9 3D models and other assets in the artwork. The layer will be used to switch to the image of each model as each of it is unlocked. This only layer will be rewarded to the first collector of the Master. QmNRixShd1izmF4pcgoaQas7CY9iAJRYMpwrrYC8.name: Deathless #70
QmNRixShd1izmF4pcgoaQas7CY9iAJRYMpwrrYC8.description:
In the beginning, there was nothing.

 The world was empty and void, black and grey,  shade and dusk. Nothing moved, nothing shifted, all was owned by The Dark. But nature is more powerful, more unknowable, more unpredictable, than any of us can imagine, and so one day, defying all odds, among The Dark, a child was born. One that was different. One that, they knew, was dangerous. 

Her true name is lost to history and the pages it was first written on. But us, we know her as Light, the first of the spectrum, the mother of all colours. As she grew, in strength and wisdom, The Dark grew more afraid, more weary of this new child in their ranks. It was why till this day the shadows fear the sun. 

Soon, a plan was hatched, to destroy their daughter, their abominable creation. A dagger of Obsidian was made, moulded from the darkest metals, the blackest materials, all to down their biggest threat. Sensing danger, Light did the only thing she could: she went to the mountains of Prisma, at the edge of all they knew, and jumped, scattering herself, her essence into 7 different parts. Her children. 

They were old and young, large and small, all with their different temperaments. These were the first of those who would wage war on their mother’s behalf. 

And we, called them The Deathless. 

The ones who didn’t die. 

The ones who had never lived. 
.
The Deathless is my hit 1/1 series, exploring the depth of color and their origins. In my Async genesis, I take that concept and turn it over on its head, creating, for the first time, an expansive canvas for everyone to explore the story I began three years ago.

QmNRoKx2gizp3gW2E6h2sxKobqdiZvY1EwwVHoyG.name: GrandRising #260
QmNRoKx2gizp3gW2E6h2sxKobqdiZvY1EwwVHoyG.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

QmNRwv9R1LVgEP8KSPgGmXpa8kBcJBev5V4hJVCC.name: Deathless #54
QmNRwv9R1LVgEP8KSPgGmXpa8kBcJBev5V4hJVCC.description:
In the beginning, there was nothing.

 The world was empty and void, black and grey,  shade and dusk. Nothing moved, nothing shifted, all was owned by The Dark. But nature is more powerful, more unknowable, more unpredictable, than any of us can imagine, and so one day, defying all odds, among The Dark, a child was born. One that was different. One that, they knew, was dangerous. 

Her true name is lost to history and the pages it was first written on. But us, we know her as Light, the first of the spectrum, the mother of all colours. As she grew, in strength and wisdom, The Dark grew more afraid, more weary of this new child in their ranks. It was why till this day the shadows fear the sun. 

Soon, a plan was hatched, to destroy their daughter, their abominable creation. A dagger of Obsidian was made, moulded from the darkest metals, the blackest materials, all to down their biggest threat. Sensing danger, Light did the only thing she could: she went to the mountains of Prisma, at the edge of all they knew, and jumped, scattering herself, her essence into 7 different parts. Her children. 

They were old and young, large and small, all with their different temperaments. These were the first of those who would wage war on their mother’s behalf. 

And we, called them The Deathless. 

The ones who didn’t die. 

The ones who had never lived. 
.
The Deathless is my hit 1/1 series, exploring the depth of color and their origins. In my Async genesis, I take that concept and turn it over on its head, creating, for the first time, an expansive canvas for everyone to explore the story I began three years ago.

QmNT6qgHg67o618CA32FSnHxejeuFKqx5v52ZEUp.name: LEAVING Silver Edition (Mix: 312001)
QmNT6qgHg67o618CA32FSnHxejeuFKqx5v52ZEUp.description:
‘Leaving' is a dynamic musical artwork that represents a new frontier in what art and music is, and should do; an experiment in storytelling, in sonic possibilities, in the value of art, and in the relationship between audience, collector, artist and authorship. The stem owners control everything: who sings the vocal part and with what melodies; what drums underpin the performance; the melodies, and even the lyrics. All the variations made possible work together seamlessly such that the artwork includes 6400 unique compositions - not trivially different, but each one its very own song, with the potential to be anything from a piano ballad to a 1980s synth track, to a sample-heavy piece of modern electronica. Each stem-owner has the power to alter the whole master, without knowing what the other stem owners will do - collectors might collaboratively arrive at a genre by responding to each others’ choices, create a genre-spanning hybrid, or actively seek out the most disharmonious composition possible.

The song explores the different states of a unique relationship between three people; a love triangle told from the perspective of all those involved. The three characters interweave and blur into each other, with the different primary emotional states as represented by the instrumental, and the different sides of the story as told by the lyrics, intermingling with unpredictable results - eventually, past present, and future; the betrayed, the betrayer and the object of the betrayal; loss, guilt and hope; all meld into one. In this way, the master track will dynamically reflect the intricate complexity of love and loss. Each individual part has been separately written, performed and recorded in a decentralised fashion by HMLTD and our collaborators, Tallulah Eden and Seth Evans. Each unique composition is a snapshot of a different angle of the love triangle in both time and perspective. The accompanying cover art, beautifully rendered by our collaborator Mike Raymond, is the visual representation of ‘Leaving'. Each possible composition; each distinct moment in the relationship, has a corresponding and distinct visual representation: three lovers, 6400 different dances, spinning and looping around in eternity.

The honey badger will give a visual cue of what vocal track is selected by the positioning of its head, while the background is determined by the selected music state change. The drum machine lies beneath the badger as it bangs on the analog buttons to create the percussion for each track. The honey badger is an early mascot in the ₿itcoin world, and represents the unstoppable force that ₿itcoin and the entire ecosystem represents. ₿orn Unique and Kaimbr rap on the "Proof Of Work (Potomac Kings)" song, Willie Waze performs "Rug Pull" and Kane Mayfield drops in for "Cryptnology."

QmNTACj2GSw5vfdh64RP8tCvGfFg84gSuGHRcf4s.name: Danktone S1E3 #1239
QmNTACj2GSw5vfdh64RP8tCvGfFg84gSuGHRcf4s.description:
On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

QmNTrxCg32msDFniLGAEBwTvuwbhmQX5em9caBue.description:
A collection of unique, iconic, Proper Punks - the people featured in this collection were around in the early days of punk in the 1970's. Each image is a tribute to them. And also to Punk Rock, Crypto Art, Trash art, Glitch Art, Rebel Rock, Punk Art, Pop Art, Naïve Art, The Situationists, The Dadaists  and all the other underground, grass roots, music & art movements that have attempted to rock the system, affect change & champion creativity - here's to the mould-breakers. The square pegs, trying to fit into round holes. 

All art hand drawn by Angie Taylor - references taken from photographs owned by Angie Taylor or 3D models created by Angie Taylor. With the exception of the following images;

QmNU5wnaATvMr2g5sSwfpJv6sJG6S6n7XL6Hd8Fb.name: environment #3
QmNU5wnaATvMr2g5sSwfpJv6sJG6S6n7XL6Hd8Fb.description:
'journey through a landscape' is the first of a series of psycho-geographical explorations.

Leaving your usual pattern and sensing of your surroundings behind, concentrating on the next potential in sonic events. Capturing moments in time and space, furthering your knowledge of the environment you inhabit with your presence. How will the overall experience of a space differ from your everyday passing by? Which new discoveries can be made, what can be learned from giving light to specific senses and being driven by the joy of sound?

This work is the result of a two hour walk through the east of Berlin in the afternoon of Thursday, 23.02.2023. It was a cold and windy day, sometimes little sun between many clouds. Recording 3 places for 15 minutes. For each place, four different compositions from the field recordings were made, resulting in 12 x 2 minute compositions. The experience was additionally archived through hand drawn sound maps. 

Every mint will be a unique combination of the sound environments and maps.

*headphones or good speaker setup highly recommended (to get the most of the spatial experience)*

QmNUTCWAPSjiJ6CCKsSjmVKsfcBJnzVS3ticuBWH.name: GrandRising #386
QmNUTCWAPSjiJ6CCKsSjmVKsfcBJnzVS3ticuBWH.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

QmNUi92nTn5DdKXmtNcELhyPmmFhuLDP4p55xEJC.name: Seaship #8
QmNUi92nTn5DdKXmtNcELhyPmmFhuLDP4p55xEJC.description:
2023 Leagues Under the Sea in the second in a series of digital colleges exploring and developing my vision of what The Metaverse (as a place to inhabit) means to me. I am a worldbuilder and storyteller, and these works enable me to envision the possibilities for its appearance, which heretofore has existed only in my imagination. Through the process of creation, a three dimensional world takes shape,emerging out of a wholly individual personal perspective which then becomes visible to others, when presented in digital form.

In the first project, I discovered that for me, The Metaverse exists in the ether, formless and invisible in the space Between Dimensions. In this project, I embark an undersea voyage seeking to expand and build upon that vision.

On my journey, I discovered that the leagues under the sea are one of the least explored expanses on Earth. There are no acres to build upon, no air to breathe. There is only soundlessness and frigid darkness in depths that are lacking in highways and byways, where predators glide freely in multiple directions, appearing silently out of the cold blackness in front of your face like weightless ghosts. 

There is an enormous sensation of a lack of control over one's environment and one's circumstances. How similar this feeling is to the one I've been having in response to the destruction and havoc wrought upon the space in the past several months. How similar the feeling of drowning. 

And yet, in the feeling of drowning, there is treasure to be found. Venturing into the depths changes you. And, unlike the world beneath the seas, and most importantly, The Metaverse is built on the foundation of an ethos that cannot be buried by either the incoming tides nor the shifting sands. 

Featuring a bunch of punks (and a seasick pepe) by cryptoartists Eric Rhodes @ericprhodes, Brandon Walsh @NFTWannabe, acid star @acidstarart and janestik.wtf @janestik

QmNUz9XYAmNdivtT7iXmyULzm2i6zfm5ewtH1cFh.name: Danktone S1E3 #266
QmNUz9XYAmNdivtT7iXmyULzm2i6zfm5ewtH1cFh.description:
On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft.

QmNVUy4GnEmkSLDKoS6bZZMV33qnZjtzQiZP5mRH.description:
In this episode of The Dankness, we dive into the world of C3, an artist who continues to push boundaries and risks it all to give a voice to the voiceless. Despite the strict anti-regime and crypto bans in Iran, C3's work has found its way into the hands of loyal collectors worldwide.  The Iranian-born enigmatic artist defies danger to share his powerful message through art and NFTs. We explore his journey from a regular job to becoming a successful full-time NFT artist, and the darkness and hardships he faced along the way.

Join us as we discuss C3's discovery of NFTs, his commitment to sharing the true stories behind his art, and the high stakes he faces in Iran for producing his work. Learn about the importance of building a cohesive body of work and how C3's kindness and empathy have shaped his experiences in the NFT space. Listen in as he shares valuable advice for new artists entering the world of NFTs and how forming genuine connections with like-minded individuals can make all the difference. You can learn more about C3 and his work at his website (c3naa.art) and be sure to follow him on Twitter @c3naaX.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft.

Every episode comes with a free collectible audio/visual NFT created through a collaboration of our bandleader and audio wizard Stella (@stellaphonic) and visionary digital artist FFFFlood (@fffflood) on Async art. We call them “Danktones” and they will be available as an open edition for a limited time after each episode. Head on over to thedankness.xyz to find out more.

Carlos is not one to shy away from speaking his mind, and his straightforward and unapologetic approach to art and life is what makes him one of our favorite people in the digital art space. You need to follow Carlos at @carlosmarcialt on Twitter and you can find some of his best work on SuperRare at superrare.com/carlosmarcial.

Before we dive in with Carlos, Dan and Jason talk Meme Wars, what it’s like to make a documentary about crypto art, and the influx of prompt-driven AI art. So buckle up, because this episode is going to be a wild ride!

QmNWNnzQ3FBBVLoXxB566AuCMmPsDLNDQw6w3qco.name: 3x3 #152
QmNWNnzQ3FBBVLoXxB566AuCMmPsDLNDQw6w3qco.description:
Named for the blend mode that inspired its creation, 'Multiply' makes liberal use of this digital composition method in its construction.

This piece consists of several hand-painted layers that overlap and mask each other in various ways. Each new 3x3 grid of colour reacts with those that came before it, before being wrapped in additional tone, border, and texture. The finished, fully-blended artwork has almost 50 billion unique possible combinations.

All artwork is 3840x3840 pixel resolution, and 5250 × 5250 'originals' are available to edition owners on request.

QmNX4ySRFHAKaFpzGyAJB3ABgbvmyEaDjrpmtD4y.name: Say It's Possible Silver Edition (Mix: 10122)
QmNX4ySRFHAKaFpzGyAJB3ABgbvmyEaDjrpmtD4y.description:
15 years ago I wrote a song called “Say It’s Possible,” and the song changed my life. 

I went from an unknown artist to the most subscribed musician on YouTube at the time. Thousands of people around the world created their own cover videos of my song. I won the inaugural YouTube Award for Best Music Video, signed deals with Universal Music Publishing and Island Records, played solo at Wembley Stadium, toured all over Europe and the UK. My experience in the major label music industry was a whirlwind ride that ultimately did not serve my best interests, and it took years of dismantling, reprogramming, and letting go of painful experiences and toxic relationships in order to find my way back to my pure love of music and the joy that comes from sharing it. 

This year I reclaimed the rights to my earliest songs from Universal Music, with the intention of recording new versions and giving these songs a life they never had. I am starting with my Async Music project: an interactive, collaborative version of my song "Say It's Possible." There are 460 possible configurations of the song and corresponding visual art, ranging from pure acoustic guitar and vocals to a lush arrangement with 13 different layers of sound.

I wrote, played, and recorded all of the music in my home studio, creating the parts in a modular way, like a puzzle, knowing the track would have to make sense in any configuration. My dear friend MG O’Shea helped with the mix, carving out frequencies to ensure all the parts would sound excellent together, in any combination. Every mix begins in the same way, like the song itself began, with acoustic guitar and vocals, evolving into something more after the first verse. Some of the changes can be subtle and some can be striking. 

The visual art is a series of self-portraits I created in the process of freeing myself from the expectations and demands placed on me by an industry that did not support me as the innovative and individualistic artist that I am.

One collector can own the Master. Up to five collectors of the individual stems (vocals, guitar, drums + percussion, bass + strings, bells + synths) will control the master mix and album cover art. A limited number of “blank records”(2,000 silver, 10 gold, 3 platinum) are also available. You can collect a blank record in advance and mint your version as soon as you hear something you love. And if you do hear something you love, mint it at that time, because we might never stumble upon that particular mix again! 

These song versions and cover art will not be released anywhere outside of this project, and the NFT you collect will be a rare and unique piece of my history and evolution as a self-actualized, independent artist.

On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

QmNXPqyNYChKb3TThscUnN8KaXdo2YZWyMCoraKw.name: GrandRising #267
QmNXPqyNYChKb3TThscUnN8KaXdo2YZWyMCoraKw.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

QmNYjkJVLHBCWXLoxobfRsESmoYoZeyKacBUDPcy.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

QmNYw821drNeCTihgniTSmdo6crriJxL4z8DEs7c.name: Danktone S1E3 #319
QmNYw821drNeCTihgniTSmdo6crriJxL4z8DEs7c.description:
On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft.

QmNZGUTDqEw92RjikLi554FcqDfUWRKsqFGV5We4.name: Inaccessible Worlds
QmNZGUTDqEw92RjikLi554FcqDfUWRKsqFGV5We4.description:
When a game fails, sometimes mid-crash you get a glimpse of a place that cannot persist. Sometimes if you manipulate some variables just right, you can teleport yourself into places that are walled-off from our experience by a barrier of cascading failure, corrupted worlds propped up by machinery that is whirring and overheating and dissipating fast as we try to take in the reality that is sliding back into the void.

These are glimpses of worlds that don't function, visions of places and times that could not persist as they were and are instead captured as still frames. This is satisfying the urge to take that glimpse of a beautiful failure and keep it - to crystallize into a transitory vision of a beautiful collapse.

More precisely - these are collections of pixels from manipulated NES games. Changing the hex code and crossing states with other games, repeating, stacking saves and layouts. Inaccessible Worlds is a broad project featuring different versions of the worlds, different formats of the art and conceptual work.

QmNae6JLkzqwf7MSyjjtQH2aV7S5CGwNZgnWKFiG.name: Deathless #41
QmNae6JLkzqwf7MSyjjtQH2aV7S5CGwNZgnWKFiG.description:
In the beginning, there was nothing.

 The world was empty and void, black and grey,  shade and dusk. Nothing moved, nothing shifted, all was owned by The Dark. But nature is more powerful, more unknowable, more unpredictable, than any of us can imagine, and so one day, defying all odds, among The Dark, a child was born. One that was different. One that, they knew, was dangerous. 

Her true name is lost to history and the pages it was first written on. But us, we know her as Light, the first of the spectrum, the mother of all colours. As she grew, in strength and wisdom, The Dark grew more afraid, more weary of this new child in their ranks. It was why till this day the shadows fear the sun. 

Soon, a plan was hatched, to destroy their daughter, their abominable creation. A dagger of Obsidian was made, moulded from the darkest metals, the blackest materials, all to down their biggest threat. Sensing danger, Light did the only thing she could: she went to the mountains of Prisma, at the edge of all they knew, and jumped, scattering herself, her essence into 7 different parts. Her children. 

They were old and young, large and small, all with their different temperaments. These were the first of those who would wage war on their mother’s behalf. 

And we, called them The Deathless. 

The ones who didn’t die. 

The ones who had never lived. 
.
The Deathless is my hit 1/1 series, exploring the depth of color and their origins. In my Async genesis, I take that concept and turn it over on its head, creating, for the first time, an expansive canvas for everyone to explore the story I began three years ago.

QmNb3Ww8wyGmpsK3RdUdZnJ3msq7Eu42XvrWYoz2.name: Danktone S1E3 #1163
QmNb3Ww8wyGmpsK3RdUdZnJ3msq7Eu42XvrWYoz2.description:
On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft.

QmNbkRZxD8mvLuWgPzfQe9nKenBEpCSbQm6C4EZr.name: GrandRising #200
QmNbkRZxD8mvLuWgPzfQe9nKenBEpCSbQm6C4EZr.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

Never have I shifted my focus so much in such a short time. Web3 and NFTs have opened my mind to so many creative possibilities I’ve never experienced before. Some days I only feel excitement, and other days I feel uncertainty as we all embark on this new adventure — but I am all in. Horizons was inspired by Async’s #AsyncNewDawn contest. There are two musical compositions, both hopeful in the end, each reflecting one of those conflicting feelings. The colors and overlays in the original art are also tied to the moods. Both musical pieces make perfect soundscapes for photo collages, YouTube or Instagram videos, etc. As with all creations by me or my family, being a holder grants you early access to future drops and future token-gated experiences.

QmNcEAJwZtA6KzCVsNeEKthbt7hxP2xFe7nDRiSV.name: Inaccessible World #360
QmNcEAJwZtA6KzCVsNeEKthbt7hxP2xFe7nDRiSV.description:
When a game fails, sometimes mid-crash you get a glimpse of a place that cannot persist. Sometimes if you manipulate some variables just right, you can teleport yourself into places that are walled-off from our experience by a barrier of cascading failure, corrupted worlds propped up by machinery that is whirring and overheating and dissipating fast as we try to take in the reality that is sliding back into the void.

These are glimpses of worlds that don't function, visions of places and times that could not persist as they were and are instead captured as still frames. This is satisfying the urge to take that glimpse of a beautiful failure and keep it - to crystallize into a transitory vision of a beautiful collapse.

More precisely - these are collections of pixels from manipulated NES games. Changing the hex code and crossing states with other games, repeating, stacking saves and layouts. Inaccessible Worlds is a broad project featuring different versions of the worlds, different formats of the art and conceptual work.

This project blends a bit of our meme culture and taps into the ancient craft of painting at the same time. It refers to our current financial state and brings an ode to artists I admire. 

When this blueprint is sold out, I will determine a date on which I will give away 'My two Satoshi's' : 
https://superrare.com/artwork-v2/'my-2-satoshis'-18110 + this particular panel to one lucky collector. 

I will use 'Wheel of Names' to pick a winner. 

To qualify for this draft, a collector needs to :

1: follow me on Twitter
2: add the address that holds the blueprint to a dedicated tweet that will be send into the world when the time is right. 


This blueprint also contains 3 legendaries which are part of the 'Bitcoin White Paper' series. This series will have 13 pieces that will be minted during 2023, more info can be found on the website.

Thank you for following me on this journey. 

May the SATS be with you!

QmNcMwknwbEW598xPRwTWwnDpJ5c1FsqUPVC5bkH.name: DANKTONE S1E4 #109
QmNcMwknwbEW598xPRwTWwnDpJ5c1FsqUPVC5bkH.description:
Welcome back to The Dankness, your go-to destination for all things crypto art and culture. This week, we've got a special guest that's going to blow your mind. Carlos Marcial is an amazing 3D artist, known for his infinitely looping masterpieces that tackle themes of governmental power and corruption. His work celebrates decentralized currency and crypto culture and it often contains reference to 20th-century art and artists.

In this episode, Carlos opens up about balancing his art career with the responsibilities of being a husband and a dad, and how crypto art has opened up doors for him that were previously closed in the traditional art world. He's also teaching himself to code and has a new generative art project in the works that's sure to make waves 🐚

Carlos is not one to shy away from speaking his mind, and his straightforward and unapologetic approach to art and life is what makes him one of our favorite people in the digital art space. You need to follow Carlos at @carlosmarcialt on Twitter and you can find some of his best work on SuperRare at superrare.com/carlosmarcial.

Before we dive in with Carlos, Dan and Jason talk Meme Wars, what it’s like to make a documentary about crypto art, and the influx of prompt-driven AI art. So buckle up, because this episode is going to be a wild ride! 

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. QmNcwcSkofDWZhmo7ZsUP961YC2YbSvt15LTYBN1.description:
Named for the blend mode that inspired its creation, 'Multiply' makes liberal use of this digital composition method in its construction.

This piece consists of several hand-painted layers that overlap and mask each other in various ways. Each new 3x3 grid of colour reacts with those that came before it, before being wrapped in additional tone, border, and texture. The finished, fully-blended artwork has almost 50 billion unique possible combinations.

All artwork is 3840x3840 pixel resolution, and 5250 × 5250 'originals' are available to edition owners on request.
